newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD told not to play poker with pensions.
newsitem.headline: German SPD told not to play poker with pensions.

text.p: Germany's main trade union body and a senior representative of the country's pensioners told the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Tuesday not to put future pensions at risk by using it as a possible election issue.

Ursula Engelen-Kefer, deputy chairwoman of the German Trade Union Federation (DGB), told an SPD meeting in Bonn that if it continued to refuse talks with the government on pension reform, the result could be sharper cuts than now planned.

SPD chief Oskar Lafontaine said on Monday that his party would not be taking up an invitation by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government to discuss a planned reform intended to reduce pensions from their current 70 percent of salary.
Kohl is seeking to pass the reform into law this year, while the SPD is resisting any cut in pensions and instead proposes a different way of financing pensions payments.

Lafontaine, who said parliament was the proper place for a debate on pensions, was attacked by officials of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) for wanting to turn the reform into a campaign issue for next year's elections.

Walter Hirrlinger, president of the VdK body that represents pensioners, the handicapped and war victims, said Germans expected from politicians of both sides "a serious struggle for consensus on such a life-or-death matter".
But SPD pensions expert Ottmar Schreiner, talking in a radio interview, said people deserved to be presented with alternatives on such questions.
